version.changelog: v1.4.11 能力层收窄：构建期裁剪 CLI + 运行期白名单闸 + export 落点加固

llm.summary: This skill is mostly coherent, but it needs Review because its CLI can go beyond the advertised fixed single-ASIN action-plan workflow while using an authenticated, credit-consuming ARI API.

dimensions.detail: Bash and network access to https://ari.funewa.com are proportionate to the ARI integration, and the code validates the official HTTPS host and blocks redirects, but the API is authenticated and can consume account credits after confirmation.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No package installation or external dependency mechanism was found; the script uses Python standard library only. Setup/configure persist an ARI API key under ~/.ari/config.json with restricted permissions, which is disclosed and purpose-aligned.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions clearly require quote-before-run and user confirmation, but scope enforcement is partly prompt/documentation-based; skill-defaults only whitelists top-level commands and does not prevent workflow/focus override arguments.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The only persistence observed is local API-key storage and submitted remote tasks/reports through ARI; no startup hooks, background services, privilege escalation, remote code execution, or local destructive behavior were found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is a fixed Amazon seller action-plan workflow for one ASIN using audit/action and ops_audit, but the runtime CLI still accepts --workflow, --focus, and --competitor for operations quote/run, allowing broader product-operation or competitor-analysis requests than the main documentation advertises.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you intend to use ARI for Amazon seller review/product analysis and are comfortable storing an ARI API key locally. Check each quote before confirming paid actions, and avoid passing workflow, focus, or competitor options unless you deliberately want analysis outside the advertised single-ASIN action-plan flow.
llm.findings:
[LP1] expected: Authenticated calls to ari.funewa.com, account/balance checks, pricing, collection, and operations endpoints are real and security-relevant, but they are disclosed by the skill and constrained to the official HTTPS host with redirect blocking.
[SDI-1] unexpected: The broad account/report-management concern is partly overstated because no local report/account mutation commands are exposed, but the artifact does expose paid collection and operations commands and permits workflow/focus overrides beyond the fixed action-plan contract.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The competitorAsin field and --competitor argument are present even though the skill is described as a single-ASIN action-planning entry, making this a real under-disclosed scope expansion.
[EA2] unexpected: The cited changelog text says autoconfirm was removed, and the runtime requires --confirm for paid collection and operation runs; I did not find autonomous paid execution without confirmation.
[P9] expected: Large blank-line blocks are present in ari.py, but inspection around the reported regions found only whitespace between functions and no hidden instructions or payloads.
[SQP-1] expected: Generic allowed command names such as setup, check, status, and operations are present; they are normal CLI commands for this integration, though routing could be narrower.
[SQP-3] expected: The documentation and CLI are primarily Chinese and generated links use /zh/ paths; this is a usability/locale disclosure issue, not evidence of unsafe behavior by itself.
[AST7] expected: The dynamic getattr use is limited to the fixed attribute list asin and competitor during local validation, so it does not appear to create arbitrary attribute access risk in this context.
